A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAMT study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary materials support reliable comparison, including matching content across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original action-recognition experiments, component ablations, generalization tests, and efficiency measurements in Tables 1-4 and S5-S9.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and adds computational-cost measurements in Table S7 and feature visualizations in Figure S5.

M1.justification: The decoupled pre-training/fine-tuning procedure, TAA, GTMT, and ELSTC remain unchanged. V2 names the training losses and clarifies temporal spacing, but does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Table 1 drops the SSV2-to-SSV2 and Diving-to-Diving evaluation cases, slightly narrowing the reported scenarios. The datasets and remaining tasks are retained. Adding SSV2 and Diving to Section 4.1's source-dataset list documents experiments already present in v1.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged across the matched main and supplementary experiments. DTMV is relabeled DMSD; the corresponding reference and identical scores establish that this is the same baseline.

E3.justification: V2 extends the existing group-number evaluation with parameter counts, FLOPs, and inference latency, and adds a last-backbone-layer heatmap comparison. Table 1 averages now exclude the removed same-domain cases. Existing splits, training budgets, backbones, and episode counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 8 and Figure S5 add a qualitative feature-heatmap comparison of TAMT and CDFSL-V on K-400 and RareAct. Table S7 expands the existing group-number sensitivity analysis with computational costs; the adapter-count and parameter-sharing ablations were already present.

E5.justification: Both versions average accuracy over 10,000 inference episodes. Neither adds training-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: After removing same-domain entries, Table 1 changes TAMT's SSV2-source average from 60.15 to 57.02 and Diving-source average from 46.93 to 45.92. These reflect different averaging sets, not lower retained transfer scores. V2 also adds ELSTC cost results, including 1.6M parameters, 2.2 GFLOPs, and 3.7 ms at G=4, plus qualitative heatmap findings.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions and Equations (1)-(10), including the moment and covariance formulations, are retained. Changing support-set notation and clarifying that temporal gaps occur at intervals of G do not introduce a new derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of a first decoupled CDFSAR training paradigm, efficient local/global temporal tuning, and substantial recognition gains. The headline 13%-31% improvement claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: The new visualization discussion argues that TAMT captures more relevant semantic regions after target-domain tuning, citing the human body and phone in RareAct's 'Hammer phone' example. Existing overfitting and grouping-tradeoff interpretations remain unchanged; no substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies mean squared error for self-supervised pre-training and cross-entropy for supervised pre-training and fine-tuning, and supplies a source-code link. Section 3.3 also clarifies grouped temporal spacing. These improve documentation without establishing changed training settings.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain the same. DMSD-CDFSAR receives updated journal metadata and a corrected baseline name; it is not a newly introduced prior work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and notation edits, clarifies the supplementary hyperparameter discussion, and adds a visualization subsection. It also adds equal-contribution information, correspondence details, and acknowledgements. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V1's Table S5(b) becomes an expanded standalone Table S7 with computational-cost columns, shifting subsequent table numbering and placement. V2 adds Figure S5's feature heatmaps and makes modest sizing and layout adjustments while retaining the main figures.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reporting consistency by excluding same-domain cases from cross-domain averages, documents training losses and code access, and strengthens the existing efficiency analysis with direct cost measurements. The new heatmaps provide limited illustrative support. These are useful improvements to transparency and evidence, while the core method, retained accuracy results, and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
